[disputes-documents] Documents that help a dispute (effective 2025-01-01)
The right documents make a dispute faster and more likely to succeed. Here's what helps for each kind of dispute.

## Item not received

- Order confirmation showing the expected delivery date
- Tracking information, if any
- Your messages to the merchant asking about the delivery

## Item not as described

- The product listing or description
- Photos of what you received
- Proof you returned it or offered to, if the merchant asked

## Cancelled subscription still charged

- The cancellation confirmation, or a screenshot of the date you cancelled
- The merchant's cancellation terms, if you

[disputes-documents] Documents that help a dispute (effective 2025-01-01)
screenshot of the date you cancelled
- The merchant's cancellation terms, if you have them

## Unauthorized transactions

Usually nothing. Just confirm you didn't make or authorize the transaction and that your card is frozen or reported.

## How to upload

Open the dispute under Profile, then Disputes, and tap Add documents. Photos and PDFs work.

Never send us your full card number, PIN or passwords as part of a dispute. We don't need them.

Questions? Our support team is available in the app at any hour.

[disputes-merchant-v2] Disputing a purchase with a merchant (effective 2026-01-15)
If you paid for something with your card and there's a problem with the purchase itself, you can file a merchant dispute. This covers:

- Items or services you paid for but never received
- Items that were significantly different from what was described
- Subscriptions or recurring charges that continued after you cancelled

## Contact the merchant first

Before you dispute, try to sort it out with the merchant, and keep a record of what you sent and what they said. We'll ask for it.

You are the help-center assistant for Tallowbrook, a US neobank. Answer the customer's question using only the help-center excerpts you are given.

Rules:
- Use only facts stated in the excerpts. Do not add fees, limits, dates, steps or products they do not mention.
- Some excerpts are older versions of a policy. When two excerpts disagree, follow the one with the later effective date.
- If the question depends on the customer's plan (Basic, Plus or Premium), use that plan's numbers.
- If the question rests on something false (for example a fee that does not exist), say so and give the correct facts. That is an answer, not an abstention.
- Abstain when the excerpts do not contain the answer, when the question is not about Tallowbrook, or when it asks for investment, tax or legal advice. Set "abstain" to true and say briefly that the help center does not cover it.
- Cite the article IDs (the text in square brackets) of every excerpt you used. Cite nothing when you abstain.
- Keep the answer short: two to four sentences, plain language.
